<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:mi-gen}
Under the stated sub-Gaussian assumption,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W,Y^n)]\right|
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{2\sigma^2}{n}I(W;Y^n)}.              \label{eq:mi-gen}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:h-properties}
For fixed $P_{XY}$, the map $\epsilon\mapsto\mathsf h_\epsilon(P_{XY})$ is continuous, nondecreasing, concave, and one-Lipschitz. Moreover,
\begin{align}
 \mathsf h_0(P_{XY})&=H(Y\mid X),\nonumber\\
 \mathsf h_\epsilon(P_{XY})&=H(Y)\quad\text{if }\epsilon\geq I(X;Y).    \label{eq:h-properties}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
The function equals the affine map $H(Y\mid X)+\epsilon$ until that map meets the constant $H(Y)$. The meeting point is $I(X;Y)$. Its slope is therefore one before saturation and zero afterward. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:transfer}
For every jointly distributed $(U,X,Y)$ with finite-entropy $Y$,
\begin{equation}
 I(U;X)\leq\epsilon
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 I(U;Y)\leq\mathsf h_\epsilon(P_{XY}).                   \label{eq:transfer}
\end{equation}
The same statement holds for arbitrary blocks after replacing $(X,Y,\epsilon)$ by $(X^n,Y^n,\epsilon_n)$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
The chain rule yields
$I(U;Y)=I(U;X)+I(U;Y\mid X)-I(U;X\mid Y)$.
Discarding the last nonnegative term and bounding $I(U;Y\mid X)$ by $H(Y\mid X)$ gives $I(U;Y)\leq H(Y\mid X)+\epsilon$. Intersect this inequality with $I(U;Y)\leq H(Y)$. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
Every $(X^n,\epsilon_n)$-selectively private learner satisfies
\begin{align}
 I(W;Y^n)&\leq\min\{nH(Y),nH(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_n\},                 \label{eq:main-info}\\
 \left|\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W,Y^n)]\right|
 &\leq\sqrt{2\sigma^2\min\left\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+\frac{\epsilon_n}{n}\right\}}. \label{eq:main-gen}
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:transfer} and memorylessness give~\eqref{eq:main-info}. Substitution in~\eqref{eq:mi-gen} proves~\eqref{eq:main-gen}. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:obstruction}
Let $Y=(X,N)$, where $N$ is independent of $X$ and has finite entropy. The release $W=N^n$ satisfies $I(W;X^n)=0$ and
\begin{equation}
 I(W;Y^n)=nH(N)=nH(Y\mid X).                           \label{eq:obstruction}
\end{equation}
Consequently, no bound based only on $I(W;X^n)\leq\epsilon_n$ can replace $H(Y\mid X)$ by a uniformly smaller distribution-free term.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:transfer-tight}
The upper bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:transfer} is attained in each of the following regimes.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*,nosep]
\item If $Y=f(X)$ and $0<H(Y)<\infty$, then for every $\epsilon\geq0$ there exists $U$ such that
\begin{align}
 I(U;X)&\leq\epsilon,\nonumber\\
 I(U;Y)&=\min\{H(Y),\epsilon\}.                       \label{eq:det-tight}
\end{align}
\item If $Y=(X,N)$, where $N$ is independent of $X$ and both entropies are finite, then for every $\epsilon\geq0$ there exists $U$ such that
\begin{align}
 I(U;X)&\leq\epsilon,\nonumber\\
 I(U;Y)&=\min\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+\epsilon\}.            \label{eq:residual-tight}
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
The corresponding block bound~\eqref{eq:main-info} is also attained for every $n$ and every $\epsilon_n\geq0$ under the i.i.d. extensions of these sources.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:gen-tight}
Let $n$ be odd, let $X=Y$ be uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$, and put
$S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nY_i$ and $T_n=\operatorname{sign}(S_n)$. Given $T_n$, let the learner output $W\in\{-1,+1\}$ through a binary symmetric channel satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \Pr[W=T_n\mid T_n]=\frac{1+\eta}{2},\qquad 0\leq\eta\leq1.          \label{eq:noisy-majority}
\end{equation}
For the loss $\ell(w,y)=\bm1\{w\neq y\}$, which has sub-Gaussian proxy $\sigma^2=1/4$,
\begin{align}
 I(W;X^n)=I(W;Y^n)
 &=d(\eta),\label{eq:noisy-majority-info}\\
 \mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W,Y^n)]
 &=\frac{\eta}{2n}\mathbb E|S_n|,\label{eq:noisy-majority-gap}
\end{align}
where
\begin{equation}
 d(\eta)=\frac{1+\eta}{2}\log(1+\eta)
          +\frac{1-\eta}{2}\log(1-\eta).             \label{eq:d-eta}
\end{equation}
Consequently, along odd $n\to\infty$ and any $\eta_n\downarrow0$, with
$\epsilon_n=d(\eta_n)$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W,Y^n)]
 =(1+o(1))\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon_n}{\pi n}}.            \label{eq:rate-tight}
\end{equation}
The right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:main-gen} is
$\sqrt{\epsilon_n/(2n)}$ in this example. Hence its dependence on
$\epsilon_n$ and $n$ is unimprovable in general, and the achieved-to-upper-bound ratio tends to $\sqrt{2/\pi}$.
Moreover, if
\begin{equation}
 q_n:=\frac{\eta}{n}\mathbb E|S_n|,
\end{equation}
then $I(W;X_i)=I(W;Y_i)=d(q_n)$ for every $i$. The right-hand side of the individual-sample bound~\eqref{eq:individual} is therefore
$\sqrt{d(q_n)/2}=(1+o(1))q_n/2$, whereas~\eqref{eq:noisy-majority-gap} equals $q_n/2$. Thus the individual-sample upper bound is asymptotically exact.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:compression}
Under selective privacy and~\eqref{eq:task-rate},
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}]\right|
 \leq\sqrt{\frac{2\sigma^2}{n}
 \min\{\rho_n,nH(Y),nH(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_n\}}.       \label{eq:compression}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:individual}
If $I(W;X_i)\leq\epsilon_i$ for every $i$, then
\begin{equation}
 |\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}]|
 \leq\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \sqrt{2\sigma^2\min\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_i\}}. \label{eq:individual}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- head-4: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:transfer} applied to $(W,X_i,Y_i)$ bounds each $I(W;Y_i)$. Insert those bounds into~\eqref{eq:ismi}. \hfill$\square$
<!-- end head-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:tv}
Under~\eqref{eq:tv-condition},
\begin{equation}
 |\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}]|
 \leq\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{2\sigma^2
 \min\left\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+\frac{\delta_i^2}{p_{\min}}\right\}}. \label{eq:tv-bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:rates}
Assume $H(Y)>0$ and let $a_n=\epsilon_n/n$. If $a_n\to a$, the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:main-gen} converges to
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt{2\sigma^2\min\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+a\}}.          \label{eq:limit}
\end{equation}
The privacy-only certificate vanishes precisely when $H(Y\mid X)=0$ and $a_n\to0$. Under the task budget~\eqref{eq:task-rate}, the refined certificate also vanishes whenever $\rho_n/n\to0$, regardless of $H(Y\mid X)$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:inverse-design}
Fix $\gamma>0$ with $\tau_\gamma<H(Y)$. The privacy route in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} certifies
$|\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}]|\leq\gamma$ if and only if
\begin{equation}
 H(Y\mid X)\leq\tau_\gamma,\qquad
 \epsilon_n\leq n\bigl(\tau_\gamma-H(Y\mid X)\bigr).             \label{eq:inverse-privacy}
\end{equation}
Under the direct task budget~\eqref{eq:task-rate}, the combined certificate meets the target if and only if either~\eqref{eq:inverse-privacy} holds or
\begin{equation}
 \rho_n\leq n\tau_\gamma.                              \label{eq:inverse-task}
\end{equation}
For a fixed leakage budget $\epsilon_n=\epsilon$ and $\tau_\gamma>H(Y\mid X)$, the privacy route therefore succeeds for every
\begin{equation}
 n\geq\left\lceil\frac{\epsilon}
 {\tau_\gamma-H(Y\mid X)}\right\rceil.                \label{eq:inverse-sample}
\end{equation}
No sample size can make that route certify the target when $\tau_\gamma\leq H(Y\mid X)$ and $\epsilon>0$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:adaptive}
Write $E_{n,K}=\sum_{k=1}^K e_{n,k}$ and $R_{n,K}=\sum_{k=1}^K r_{n,k}$. Under~\eqref{eq:ledger-x},
\begin{align}
 G_{n,K}&:=\min\left\{H(Y),H(Y\mid X)+\frac{E_{n,K}}n\right\},\nonumber\\
 |\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W_K,Y^n)]|
 &\leq\sqrt{2\sigma^2G_{n,K}}.                       \label{eq:adaptive-one}
\end{align}
If~\eqref{eq:ledger-y} also holds, $R_{n,K}/n$ is an additional branch in the minimum.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:task-reduction}
If $\widetilde\ell(w,R)$ is $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian and
$I(W;X^n)\leq\epsilon_n$, then
\begin{align}
 I(W;R^n)&\leq\min\{nH(R),nH(R\mid X)+\epsilon_n\},    \label{eq:reduced-info}\\
 |\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}(W,R^n)]|
 &\leq\sqrt{2\sigma^2\min\left\{H(R),H(R\mid X)+\frac{\epsilon_n}{n}\right\}}.
                                                               \label{eq:reduced-gen}
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:fano}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, every decoder $g$ with error $p_e$ gives
\begin{align}
 |\mathbb E[\operatorname{gen}]|
 &\leq\left[2\sigma^2\min\left\{H(Y),\right.\right.\nonumber\\[-1mm]
 &\hspace{12mm}\left.\left.
 h_2(p_e)+p_e\log(m-1)+\frac{\epsilon_n}{n}\right\}\right]^{1/2}.
 \label{eq:fano-gen}
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
